Root and template parity is proved by blob id, not only by diff: all three pairs share one blob (implementer.md 1d88113, task-reviewer.md 01079be, orchestrating/SKILL.md a944598), and no generated artifact moved because no knowledge file changed.

issues.what: The audit's process.evals-rerun row fails at this head: .claude/agents/implementer.md and .claude/agents/task-reviewer.md changed without .claude/evals/record.json.
issues.why: The scenarios in .claude/evals/ are the regression suite for the agent templates. Until a run set covers these template blobs, no evidence says the four new sentences steer an implementer and a reviewer as intended.
issues.fix: Invariant to hold: no branch merges while a template blob has no evaluation run set covering it. Observed instance: this task's range changes both agent templates and appends no record. Make no change in this task: the spec schedules T3, `docs(evals): seventh evaluation record`, to run every scenario at the branch head and key the record by both template blob ids, and the branch-range audit is the row that must pass before the merge.

issues.what: The new clause "`output` carries the command's stdout and stderr verbatim and nothing else, the `exit` field alone carries the exit status" sits in the `live_run` bullet only. The batch 13 T2 incident it encodes appended the same synthetic `exit=0` line inside fix_rounds[0].tests[2..4] as well as inside live_run[10..21]; I confirmed both in .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-03-batch-13/task-2-report.json. Line 39's `tests` bullet still carries only the bare word "verbatim", which is the wording those fix-round captures already violated.
issues.why: The recurrence the sentence is meant to make impossible stays possible in `tests` and `fix_rounds[].tests`, where three of the five synthetic lines actually appeared. An evidence field that mixes a command's output with the author's annotation cannot be trusted, whichever field it is.
issues.fix: Invariant to hold: every report field that carries captured output holds what the command printed and nothing else, and the exit status lives only in an `exit` field, in `tests` and `fix_rounds[].tests` as well as `live_run`. Observed instance: template/.claude/agents/implementer.md:40 carries the clause in the `live_run` bullet while line 39 keeps only "verbatim". Extend the clause to the `tests` bullet, or state it once for both bullets; if the batch defers it, file a backlog item and name it in the deferral.

issues.what: Item 6 mandates the comparison but names no disposition for a mismatch: "confirm the report's `fix_rounds` findings list matches the findings under verification one for one". A re-review has no `issues` array, so item 4's "file every fail under `issues`" does not reach it, and the Output section's re-review fields (finding_verdicts, new_breakage, out_of_scope, verdict) are not named here. In batch 13 T2 round 1 the mismatch was in fact noticed and left in prose, which is the failure HR-050 names.
issues.why: The sentence closes the "nobody compared the lists" hole and leaves the "compared them and recorded nothing enforceable" hole open, so the same report defect can still pass a round with a prose mention. Read literally it also suggests a short list alone blocks `all-addressed`, which would mislabel a round whose findings are every one fixed.
issues.fix: Invariant to hold: a mismatch between the report's `fix_rounds` findings list and the findings under verification is recorded where the implementer must act on it, and it does not by itself reopen findings that are fixed. Observed instance: template/.claude/agents/task-reviewer.md:27 states the check with no destination and no ruling. Name the destination (`new_breakage`) and the ruling in the sentence; if the batch defers it, file a backlog item and name it in the deferral.

issues.what: `tdd` is `[]` with no line that discloses why. The brief asks for "`tdd` [] with the disclosure", and every earlier docs-only report in the workspace carries one (batch 13 T2: "tdd is [] by disclosure: every changed file is prose ..."; batches 4, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 the same). self_review[4] says no code was touched, but it argues doc-comments; the commit body's "Data-only." is not the report.
issues.why: process.tdd calls an empty tdd honest only when the gates that replace RED and GREEN are named as the stand-in. Without the sentence a reader must infer the claim, and the branch review re-derives it.
issues.fix: Invariant to hold: a report with an empty `tdd` states in self_review or concerns that the change is data-only or docs-only and names the gates in `tests` that stand in for RED and GREEN. Observed instance: task-2-report.json carries `tdd: []` and no such sentence in either field. Add the disclosure line, naming the gates that ran.

assessment.text: The four sentences are right, well placed, and provably generic, and the evidence behind them is trustworthy. I ran the audit with the dispatch's nine Knowledge ids verbatim (--base 2fde017 --head c081df4 --report the task report): 10 deterministic rows, 9 pass, 1 fail, 0 skipped, and I judged all 26 open rows to pass. The report validates and its self_audit reproduces my audit row for row, with no row omitted or altered. I verified each sentence against the incident it encodes by reading the archives, not the report's account of them: batch 11 T2 round 0's prescription ("present but not a string raises UsageError") is exactly the letter-fix the new Calibration sentence now forbids, and batch 13 T2's four-of-five fix_rounds list against its five finding_verdicts is what item 6 now forces a reviewer to compare. I reproduced the fresh-install proofs myself: a scratch `init` ships all four sentences, the negative grep over the three installed files matches nothing, and both cited knowledge ids plus the `fix_rounds.findings` field resolve in the seed. All three template/root pairs share one blob id. The live-run captures still exist and match the report byte for byte, and none appends a synthetic exit line, which is the rule this task ships. The process.evals-rerun fail is the interim state the rule's own last paragraph allows and the spec schedules onto T3; I filed it as the mandatory issue for a fail row with plan_mandated set and HR-050 named, and it needs no change in this task. Three Minors remain: the verbatim-output clause covers `live_run` but not the `tests` and `fix_rounds[].tests` captures that carried three of the batch 13 synthetic lines; item 6 states the check but no disposition for a mismatch, so the defect it targets can still end in prose; and the report omits the empty-tdd disclosure the brief asks for. One thing I considered and cleared: the live_run clause joins two independent statements with a comma rather than the spec's semicolon, which is forced by the bullet's existing semicolon separators and reads unambiguously.
